questions.q: Which interface has exactly one abstract method and can therefore be the target of a lambda?
o: Any interface with default methods only
Any abstract class with one method
questions.w: The rule is one abstract method. Default and static methods, and re-declared `Object` methods, do not count.

questions.q: Which functional interface takes no argument and returns a value?
questions.w: Supplier: `() -> T`. Consumer: `T -> void`. Predicate: `T -> boolean`. Function: `T -> R`.

questions.q: What does this code do? `int count = 0; list.forEach(x -> count++);`
o: It does not compile: captured locals must be effectively final
It counts the elements of the list correctly
It counts correctly, but only on one thread
It throws an exception when the lambda runs
questions.w: A lambda captures a copy of the value, so the local cannot change. Use `list.size()`, `stream().count()` or an `AtomicInteger`.

questions.q: What does `this` refer to inside a lambda body?
o: The enclosing object, as in the surrounding method
questions.w: An anonymous inner class has its own `this`. A lambda does not introduce a new scope for `this`.

questions.q: What is the difference between `orElse(x)` and `orElseGet(supplier)` on an `Optional`?
o: `orElse` always evaluates `x`, `orElseGet` calls the supplier only when empty
`orElseGet` always evaluates its argument, `orElse` does not
They are identical, only the names differ
questions.w: With `orElse(createDefault())` the default is built even when a value is present. Prefer `orElseGet` for anything expensive.

As a field type in a JPA entity
As a method parameter that callers may skip
As the element type of a `List`
questions.w: It was designed for return values. For fields and parameters use plain types, overloads or validation; for no results, return an empty collection.

questions.q: `find(id).map(this::findBranch)` where `findBranch` itself returns an `Optional<Branch>`. What type results, and what is the better call?
questions.w: `map` wraps the function's result. `flatMap` expects the function to return an `Optional` and does not wrap it again.

questions.q: How is `Predicate<Account> p = a -> a.isActive();` best combined with another predicate `q`?
questions.w: `Predicate` has `and`, `or` and `negate`. `Function` has `andThen` and `compose`. Compose small named pieces instead of one long lambda.
